title: StreamEventBase
description: The fields every stream event may carry. A finding and a stand-aside phase event add SignalMeta; a subcommittee event adds Subcommittee.

type.description: connected: the stream is open. heartbeat: keeps the connection open. error: the stream cannot continue. thread_found: the thread answering this turn, by threadId. phase: an agent's progress. finding: an agent's consensus signal. subcommittee: the agents the coordinator convened. activity: who is busy on the thread now. synthesis: the answer, in content. done: the thread closed.

agent.description: The agent a phase, finding or subcommittee event is about.

status.description: The phase: waking, ready, triaging, evaluating, waiting, or done for an agent that stood aside.

gpu.description: The accelerator the agent runs on.

signal.description: The consensus signal of a finding (agree, concern, block or failure), or stand_aside on the stand-aside phase event.

summary.description: The first line of a finding, or a concern's text.

content.description: A finding's full contribution, or the synthesis.

stood_aside.description: Set on the phase event of an agent that stood aside.

model.description: The model a waiting agent waits for.

reason.description: Why an agent waits or stood aside, such as gpu-busy.

at.description: When an activity event was taken, RFC 3339 in UTC.

receipt.description: On done, the DiscussionReceipt of discussion-metadata.json exactly as the thread_close message carried it: what the thread cost and how it went, including every model call the scheduler placed with its prediction and what the call measured. Absent when the closing message carried none.

timestamp.description: When the discussion message behind the event was published, RFC 3339 in UTC. Events the gateway makes up itself carry none.
